name: Observability & Debuggability
checks: All logs are JSON format with `trace_id` / `correlation_id`
Core paths (auth, billing, generation, data mutation) have structured success/failure logs
Errors include stack trace + request context
No PII or secrets in logs
Every request/task has a trackable ID (`trace_id`, `x-request-id`, `run_id`)
Production does NOT rely solely on unstructured `console.log`
Background jobs/workers produce unique `run_id` per execution
External dependency calls log: response time, status code, retry count
Failure paths have explicit instrumentation (not just generic error log)
Log event names are specific and stable (no `something happened`)
Debuggability does not depend on local reproduction only — production issues can be diagnosed from logs/traces/metrics without requiring local environment recreation

Upstream observability plan items have corresponding literal emit calls — events / trace identifiers declared in Step 1 Observability Plan are grep-verifiable in implementation code as literal `logger.*(<event_name>, ...)` / equivalent emit calls (see DEBUGGING_OBSERVABILITY_GUIDELINE §6A.5 Plan Literal-Match Rule)
High-risk flows have alert rules — critical paths (auth failure spikes, payment errors, data mutation failures) trigger automated alerts [SHOULD]
Key operations have Span recording — important operations emit distributed tracing spans with timing and metadata [SHOULD]
Cross-service requests are traceable end-to-end — trace IDs propagate across service boundaries for full request lifecycle visibility [SHOULD]
Log drain configured to external platform — logs shipped to external aggregation platform (not only local disk) [SHOULD]
Frontend Real User Monitoring (RUM) — when project has user-facing frontend
External dependency monitoring — when project depends on third-party services
Health check endpoint — when project is a deployed service

checks.check: Background and worker paths can answer: did it start, did it run twice, which step failed, and did checkpoint, retry and cleanup behave as intended.
Logs distinguish provider failure from local failure.
Trace context is injected by middleware, not added by hand in each handler.
External writes leave an audit trail: actor, timestamp, trace id.
checks.why_not_a_checker: 要知邊個算 actor、邊個算 trace id，係逐個 repo 嘅詞彙。而 X/Y 實驗顯示呢條喺前閘度 25 次曝光只換到 2 句提及，喺後閘度提出 6 次兩臂都認真拒絕連理由 —— 佢係一個讀住 code 先諗得起嘅問題。

anti_patterns: Unstructured logs as only observability source
No correlation ID / trace ID across related events
Reactive-only debugging (add instrumentation only after incident)
High-risk paths with no visibility into inputs, outputs, failures
PII or secrets leaked in logs
Stub-as-proof: Step 5 commands_run 經 stub / placeholder ID / signature inspection / harness probe / low-level helper 旁路 production entrypoint，取代 truth-owner read-back → flag P1
Surface validation schema compliance gap: surface validation evidence commands_run 缺 schema validation script invocation；驗證 exit=0 與 PASS marker；空結果 → flag P1
why: Review guidance, not an enforced checker or proof of review completion. Apply each question to this repo’s actual scope and architecture; state when it does not apply. Source names and R-/PL- identifiers are historical attribution, not required files in the adopter. Historical measurements below describe the recorded experiment, not a new measurement.
